text:
A rain gauge is pretty basic. You just catch rain with this fixed size hole. It channels the water down through a small tube that has depth marks on it. mm or inches, so you get the reading. The reading is basically the depth the rain would be if it all fell and just stayed on the ground no running off no soak in.
So the top hole usually is bigger than the tube to get it down to a smaller column. But they calibrate the scale to the area ratio, so still the right depth.
The two big problems I see are placement and evap. If you put it next to trees or buildings or fences you'll either get too little or too much depending on if it shelters or the run off and splash will add.
And the issue is evap, if you do not read it very soon, you'll be low.
